llm.summary: This skill is a real ARI listing-analysis integration, but it can spend credits and change persistent account settings with less per-action confirmation than users may expect.

dimensions.detail: Network access, an ARI bearer key, product/review/account reads, local exports, and local credential storage are coherent with the service, but the command surface is broad for a narrowly advertised mobile-listing skill and export output paths can overwrite arbitrary writable files selected via --out.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package install or remote-code update mechanism was found; setup uses browser device authorization and saves an ARI API key locally under ~/.ari/config.json with restrictive POSIX permissions, while API traffic goes to the ARI service unless a custom base URL is explicitly enabled.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Several workflows require quotes and user confirmation, especially the fixed listing/mobile operations path, but VOC/analyze paths explicitly honor service-side autoConfirm and tell the agent not to ask before generating paid results when that flag is returned.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can persist an API key and can change long-lived account behavior such as auto-confirm thresholds, schedules, watches, competitor bindings, alert read state, and workbench review status; most are disclosed, but auto-confirm and recurring collection controls are high-impact enough to require review.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is mobile Amazon Listing diagnosis, but the shipped instructions and CLI also cover broader ARI account workflows including VOC reports, exports, alerts, competitor management, schedules, watches, workbench status updates, leaderboard queries, and confirmation settings.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It is not showing evidence of deception, exfiltration, destructive remote code, or hidden persistence, but only install it if you are comfortable giving it ARI account access, local key storage, local file export ability, and authority to run paid ARI workflows. Set auto-confirm to ask every time if you want explicit approval before spending credits, confirm the marketplace for each paid task, and avoid using --out paths that point at existing or sensitive files.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network calls, local credential storage, and CLI execution are disclosed and necessary for ARI integration, so this is not malicious by itself; the metadata does understate the operational authority exposed by the package.
[TP4] unexpected: The broad ARI CLI and instructions go beyond the public mobile-listing description. Some broader functions support listing operations, but billing, exports, monitoring, workbench, leaderboard, and account settings make the scope materially wider than advertised.
[SQP-3] expected: Defaulting to amz_us is plainly documented. It is a usability default rather than hidden behavior, but users should confirm marketplace before paid or account-affecting actions.
[EA2] unexpected: The autoConfirm behavior is artifact-backed in SKILL.md, reference.md, and scripts/ari.py: paid VOC/analyze workflows can execute without a fresh in-session confirmation when the service returns autoConfirm, and the skill instructs the agent not to ask afterward.
[T09] unexpected: Exporting reports/reviews locally is expected, but request_download writes --out with open(dest, "wb") and does not prevent overwrites or symlink following, creating a real local file-corruption risk within the user's writable filesystem.
